full_judgment:
2. The case of the petitioner is, in short, as follows: 

 The petitioner No. 1 Rehana Begum aged about 18 years is at present detained in District Jail Sylhet under Judicial Custody by an order dated 30-5-96 passed by the Magistrate. 1st Class, Moulvibazar in GR Case No. 299 of 1996 corresponding to GD No. 3042 dated 30-5-96 although she committed no crime nor there is any allegation of any offence committed by her. She has not been charged whatsoever for any crime/offence under the Penal Code or violated/breached any law in Bangladesh. The petitioner No.1 is a British citizen from an early age and has been residing in the UK with her parents and has been brought up and educated there having sat for her GCSE (equivalent to Matriculation) examination in 1995. After the examination her father persuaded the petitioner No. 1 to come on a holiday to his village home at Raipur, District Moulvibazar. Her father took away her British passport which was later to be used by him for a lucrative transaction and left for the UK leaving her in the lurch for an indefinite period. She was left behind as a commodity in the bride market to be sold out to a prospective husband. The petitioner No. 1 facing such inhuman situation, developed a fascination for her confidant, Isa Khan. Their friendship gradually deepened and blossomed further and they eventually fell in love. She then fiance to elope with her fiance Isa Khan and marry him. Accordingly, they married on 19-5-1996 which was registered on 27-5-1996 by the Nikka Registrar of Komolgonj, Moulavibazar, Sylhet. The father of the petitioner No. 1 LalMiah could not accept that his daughter in fact made an independent decision. Although there was no case of abduction filed in any police station he couple, as part of an understanding with the petitioner's father decided to surrender on 29-5-96 to the authorities of Moulvibazar Thana is good faith of likely compromise/settlement verbally assured by Rehana's father. After the surrender of the couple the officer-in-charge on 30-5-96 forwarded an application to the Magistrate, 1st Class, Moulavibazar showing the arrest of the couple under section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure being GD No. 3042 dated 30-5-96 and praying, inter alia, that Rehana Begum should be sent to judicial custody since the officer did not know what to do with her. The Magistrate on 30-5-96 sent the accused. Isa Khan to jail and sent Rehana Begum to judicial custody observing that there was no application for bail on her behalf, although she was not an accused nor witness in any case. On 1-6-96 the father of the petitioner No.1 filed a complaint case before the Magistrate 1st Class. Moulvibazar alleging that his daughter was drugged which rendered her psychologically unstable and that she was kidnapped by miscreants/robbers at the instigation of her husband Isa Khan and that his daughter was later handed over to lsa Khan who had raped her. The father further alleged that not only Rehana was in unsound mental condition due to drugs and incapable to take any decision, but that she was also a minor child, ineligible to take any decision regarding her marriage. The complaint case was lodged under Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Special Act, 1995 and under sections 366, 376, 380 and 457 of the Penal Code. Following the said complaint case the learned Magistrate made an order on 1-6-96 directing the Officer-in-Charge of Moulvibazar Police Station to treat the complaint case as an FIR Accordingly, a Police Case was started on 7-6-96 being Moulvibazar PS Case No. 3(6)96, (GR Case No. 299/96). On 2-6-96 there was cross application by both the father and the husband to release Rehana Begum in their respective custody. But the learned Magistrate recorded a finding that since the case.has been filed under relevant section of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Act, 1995, Rehana cannot be released in any one's custody. Again on 5-6-96 and 8-6-96 similar application for release of the petitioner No. 1 was made by both the father and the husband praying that she be released in their respective custody at the exclusion of the other. But the learned Magistrate refused the custody in respect of either the husband or the father. The learned Magistrate also ordered that since a regular case has been started being Case No. 3(6) 96 (GR Case No. 299/96 therefore the present case under section 54 of the CrPC vide GD No. 3042 was closed and the records were accordingly filed and amalgamated with the regular PS Case No. 3(6)96. On 9-6-96 in the regular Moulvibazar PS Case No. 3(6)96 the Investigation Officer also prayed for examination of Rehana by the doctor for determination of her age whereupon it was allowed by the Magistrate and a team of doctors examined Rehana on 10-6-96 and the Civil Surgeon submitted his report as following: 

 3. It is submitted that the petitioner No.1 has remained in jail custody since then although she is neither an accused nor a witness in any pending criminal case. She is about 18 years old and not being an accused in any criminal case or witness, her detention in Moulvibazar Jailor Sylhet Jail is illegal and without lawful authority. Hence this application. 

 4. Mr. K S Nabi, the learned Attorney General appearing for the State, has not opposed the Rule and submits that he has no objection if the petitioner No. 1 is set at liberty. Although the father of the petitioner No. 1 has not been made a party Mr Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate informed the court that there is a case pending with regard to the custody of the petitioner No.1. If the petitioner No. 1 is set free, it will prejudice the application made by the father of the petitioner No. 1 in her custody. 

 5. The present Rule relates to the question of the petitioner's No. 1 detention in Moulvibazar Jail. It appears that the petitioner No. 1 is alleged to be a victim of rape and kidnapping. She is not an accused nor a witness in any proceeding. In that view of the matter the question is whether under the circumstances she can be kept in judicial custody. In the case of Ananda Mohan Banerjee on behalf of Priti Banerjee vs State and others, reported in 35 DLR while dealing with he similar case reference was made to the case of Jahanara Begum alias Jotsna Rani Shaha vs State and another reported in 15 DLR 148 wherein it was held as follows: 

 Reference were also made to another unreported case in Criminal Revision No. 522 of 1979 decided by the Division Bench of this Court wherein it was held as follows: 

 "The decision of that case has been supported in the case of Fatema Begum @ Urmila Rani vs Gayeswar Nath and State reported in 1989 BLD 469 and in the case of Sree Tarapada Sarker Vs. The State and others, reported in 17 BLD 379. 

 6. In the instant case it appears from the Annexure-H to the petition that on a medical examination held on 10-6-96 the age of the petitioner No.1 Rehana Begum was between 15 and 16 years. So, according to that report of the Civil Surgeon she is over 16 years of age as of today. We also examined the petitioner No. 1 Rehana Begum in our chamber in the presence of her learned counsel and the Attorney General. The petitioner No. 1 Rehana Begum emphatically stated that she did not for a moment want to continue to be detained in the jail custody. She also stated that she was quite capable of taking care of herself. 

 7. In the light of above legal position and in view of the petitioner's statement we are of the view that the petitioner No.1 Rehana Begum's detention in Moulvibazar Jail is without any lawful authority and she must be set free at once. So far as Misc. Case No. 4243 of 1996 filed by the father of the petitioner No. 1 with regard to her custody is concerned that question will be decided on merit by the relevant Court and for that purpose the petitioner No.1 Rehana Begum shall not leave Bangladesh without permission of that Court.
